decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text begins chapter 6 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 5 runs on to verse 41, and its last fifteen verses (5:27-41 here), the line of the high priests, are numbered 6:1-15 in many Bibles. So this chapter's verses 1-66 are numbered 6:16-81 in those Bibles. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: Gershom: the son of Levi called Gershon in Exodus 6:16 and Numbers 3:17
decisions.reason: Levi's first son is Gershon in Genesis 46:11, Exodus 6:16, Numbers 3:17 and 1 Chronicles 5:27, but this chapter spells his name Gershom each time (verses 2, 5, 28, 47, 56). The two forms name the same man. He is not Gershom the son of Moses (Exodus 2:22).

decisions.choice: a new start: the whole tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: The list in 5:27-41 followed only the line of the high priests. Here the writer starts again from Levi's three sons, to give the other Levite families (verses 1-15), the singers David appointed (verses 16-32), and the towns the Levites lived in (verses 39-66).

decisions.choice: The sons of X: A, B and C
decisions.reason: The list formula is kept the same through these chapters. Literal and Balanced keep the bare heading with a colon, as the Hebrew does; Readable adds "were" to make a sentence.

decisions.reason: "Libni his son, Jahath his son" means Libni was Gershom's son, Jahath was Libni's son, and so on: a single line traced down from father to son. Such lists give the main links of a family line and may leave some generations out.

decisions.choice: compare the line of Asaph in verses 24-28
decisions.reason: Asaph's line in verses 24-28 also goes back to Gershom through Zimmah and Jahath, but there Shimei stands between Zimmah and Jahath, and Jahath is the son of Gershom without Libni. The two lists give different links in the same family line.

decisions.choice: "his son" kept after each name
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the repeated "his son", which shows that this is a line of descent and not a list of brothers.

decisions.choice: Amminadab: where the other lists have Izhar
decisions.reason: Korah was the son of Izhar son of Kohath (verses 22-23; Exodus 6:18, 21), so Amminadab stands here where Izhar would be expected. He may be Izhar under another name, or the name may have come in by a copying slip. He is not Amminadab of Judah, Aaron's father-in-law (Exodus 6:23).

decisions.choice: Korah: the Korah who rebelled against Moses
decisions.reason: This is the Korah of Numbers 16. His sons did not die with him (Numbers 26:11), and their descendants became singers and gatekeepers; several psalms bear the heading "of the sons of Korah" (Psalms 42; 44-49).

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: The list runs through many generations, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants"; Literal keeps "sons".

decisions.reason: Exodus 6:24 names Assir, Elkanah and Abiasaph (another spelling of Ebiasaph) as brothers, the sons of Korah. Here the "and" before Ebiasaph and Assir may mark the first three as brothers, with the line going on through Ebiasaph and his son Assir, as verse 22 has it (Tahath son of Assir son of Ebiasaph son of Korah).

decisions.reason: The scribes' marginal reading, which the vowels follow, has "the sons of Elkanah". The consonants written in the text spell "his son", which reads "Ahimoth, Elkanah his son, Elkanah: Zophai his son ..." and fits verse 20, where Elkanah is the son of Mahath (Ahimoth). Either way the line runs from Elkanah to Zophai and Nahath.

decisions.choice: Zophai and Nahath: called Zuph and Toah in verses 19-20
decisions.reason: The same ancestors appear as Zuph and Toah in Heman's line (verses 19-20), and as Zuph and Tohu in the family line of Samuel's father in 1 Samuel 1:1.

decisions.choice: Elkanah son of Jeroham: Samuel's father, as in 1 Samuel 1:1
decisions.reason: 1 Samuel 1:1 traces Samuel's father as Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph. Verses 19-20 here have Elkanah, Jeroham, Eliel, Toah, Zuph. Eliab, Eliel and Elihu are forms of the name of one ancestor.

decisions.choice: Samuel's family: Levites living in Ephraim
decisions.reason: 1 Samuel 1:1 calls Elkanah an Ephraimite, which says where the family lived. This list shows that they were Levites of Kohath's line, a branch that was given towns in Ephraim (verse 51; Joshua 21:20-22).

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Samuel: the firstborn Vashni, and Abijah.

en.L: And [the] sons of Samuel: the firstborn Vashni, and Abijah.
en.B: The sons of Samuel: Vashni the firstborn, and Abijah.
en.R: Samuel's sons were Vashni, the oldest, and Abijah.

decisions.choice: Vashni (Hebrew text); probably "the firstborn [Joel], and the second Abijah"
alternatives: the firstborn Joel, and the second Abijah
decisions.reason: 1 Samuel 8:2 says Samuel's firstborn was Joel and his second son Abijah, and verse 18 here calls Heman "son of Joel, son of Samuel". The letters of "Vashni" also spell "and the second". So it is likely that the name Joel dropped out in copying, and the verse first read "the firstborn Joel, and the second Abijah". Some ancient translations are said to name Joel here. The Hebrew text as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: Samuel: the prophet, son of Elkanah
decisions.reason: Samuel was the son of Elkanah and Hannah (1 Samuel 1:19-20), so the line of verses 11-12 leads to him. His sons were judges in Beersheba (1 Samuel 8:1-3).

source.text: בְּנֵ֥י מְרָרִ֖י מַחְלִ֑י לִבְנִ֥י בְנ֛וֹ שִׁמְעִ֥י בְנ֖וֹ עֻזָּ֥ה בְנֽוֹ׃

en.B: The descendants of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,
en.R: Merari's descendants were Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,

decisions.choice: Mahli heads the line; this Libni and Shimei are not Gershom's sons
decisions.reason: Mahli is Merari's son (verse 4), and the line goes on from him. Libni and Shimei here are later men of Merari's family who share the names of Gershom's two sons (verse 2).

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

en.L: Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.
en.B: Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.
en.R: Shimea his son, Haggiah his son and Asaiah his son.

decisions.choice: Asaiah: probably the leader of Merari's line in David's time
decisions.reason: An Asaiah led the descendants of Merari when David brought the ark to Jerusalem (15:6). If he is meant, each of the three lines in verses 5-15 reaches down to about David's time.

source.text: וְאֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶעֱמִ֥יד דָּוִ֛יד עַל־יְדֵי־שִׁ֖יר בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מִמְּנ֖וֹחַ הָאָרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are those] whom appointed David over [the] hands of song [in the] house of Yahweh, from [the] resting of the ark.

en.L: And these [are those] whom David appointed over the hands of song [in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, after the resting of the ark.
en.B: These are the men David put in charge of the singing in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} after the ark had come to rest.
en.R: After the ark had come to its resting place, David put these men in charge of the singing in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: over the hands of song: in charge of the singing
decisions.reason: "Hands" here means the charge or direction of a task, as when work is done "under the hands" of a leader (25:2-3). David set these men over the singing in worship.

decisions.choice: after the ark came to rest: when David brought it to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: David brought the ark of the LORD to Jerusalem and set it in the tent he had pitched for it (2 Samuel 6:17; 1 Chronicles 15:1; 16:1). After that the ark no longer moved from place to place, and David appointed Levites to sing and play before it (15:16-22; 16:4-7). The "resting place" of the ark is also sung of in Psalm 132:8 and 2 Chronicles 6:41.

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD: the place of the LORD's worship before the temple
decisions.reason: The temple was not yet built (verse 17). The phrase names the place where the LORD was worshiped, here the tent sanctuary, as "the house of the LORD" is used of the sanctuary at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1:7).

decisions.choice: the singing
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "song"; Balanced and Readable say "the singing", the activity these men led. Literal keeps "song".

source.text: וַיִּהְי֨וּ מְשָׁרְתִ֜ים לִפְנֵ֨י מִשְׁכַּ֤ן אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵד֙ בַּשִּׁ֔יר עַד־בְּנ֧וֹת שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיַּעַמְד֥וּ כְמִשְׁפָּטָ֖ם עַל־עֲבוֹדָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they were serving before [the] tabernacle of [the] tent of meeting with song until built Solomon the house of Yahweh in Jerusalem; and they stood according to their rule over their service.

en.L: And they were ministering before the tabernacle of the tent of meeting with song until Solomon built the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem; and they stood according to their rule for their service.
en.B: Until Solomon built the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem, they ministered with song before the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, carrying out their service in the order laid down for them.
en.R: They served with songs in front of the tabernacle, the meeting tent, until Solomon built the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem. They did their work in the way that had been set for them.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle of the tent of meeting: the tent sanctuary made under Moses
decisions.reason: The full name is used for the sanctuary Moses set up (Exodus 39:32; 40:2). In David's time the tabernacle stood at Gibeon, while the ark was in the tent David had pitched in Jerusalem (16:1, 39; 21:29). The singers served at both places (16:37-42), and here the phrase stands for the whole of that worship before the temple was built.

decisions.choice: ministering: serving in worship
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the service of priests and Levites at the sanctuary (Numbers 3:6; 1 Chronicles 16:4, 37).

decisions.choice: they stood according to their rule: they served in the prescribed order
decisions.reason: To "stand" at a task is to serve at one's post. The word for "rule" is often "judgment" or "custom"; here it is the order fixed for their work (15:13; 23:31).

decisions.choice: the meeting tent; the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says "the meeting tent" for "the tent of meeting", as elsewhere, and "temple" for the house Solomon built, as in 1 Kings 6:1. Literal and Balanced keep "house".

en.B: These are the men who served, with their sons. From the Kohathites: Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel,
en.R: These are the men who served, along with their sons. From the Kohathite clan came Heman the singer. He was the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,

decisions.choice: those standing: those who served at their posts
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, "stand" means to serve. These are the leaders of the singers, each with his sons serving under him (25:1-6).

decisions.choice: three leaders, each traced back to Levi
decisions.reason: Heman of Kohath's line stands in the middle (verses 18-23), Asaph of Gershom's line at his right (verses 24-28) and Ethan of Merari's line at his left (verses 29-32). Each line is traced up to Levi, so all three branches of the tribe share in the singing.

decisions.choice: son of Joel, son of Samuel: the grandson of the prophet Samuel
decisions.reason: Joel was Samuel's firstborn son (1 Samuel 8:2; see the note on verse 13). Heman led the singers with Asaph and Ethan (15:17, 19; 25:1). A Heman is also named in the title of Psalm 88.

decisions.choice: He was the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence for the line of ancestors, which runs on to verse 23.

decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell the name a little differently; the scribes' marginal reading, which the vowels follow, gives Zuph, the form in 1 Samuel 1:1. The meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: given: assigned, set apart for the work

decisions.choice: the tabernacle of the house of God: the sanctuary

decisions.choice: fellow Levites / The other Levites; appointed / given
decisions.reason: "Their brothers" means the rest of the tribe, so Balanced says "fellow Levites" and Readable "the other Levites". Balanced says "appointed" for the sense of "given"; Literal and Readable keep "given".

en.L: And Aaron and his sons [were] burning [offerings] on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense, for all the work of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the slave of God had commanded.
en.B: But Aaron and his sons made the offerings go up in smoke on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense. They did all the work of the Most Holy Place and made atonement for Israel, just as Moses the servant of God had commanded.
en.R: But Aaron and his sons burned the offerings on the altar for burnt offerings and burned incense on the incense altar. They did all the work in the Most Holy Place and made atonement for Israel. They did everything just as Moses, the servant of God, had commanded.

decisions.choice: and Aaron: set against the Levites of verse 33
decisions.reason: The Levites served the sanctuary, but the work at the altars and in the holy place belonged to Aaron and his descendants alone (Numbers 18:1-7).

decisions.choice: making smoke: burning offerings so that they go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb covers both altars: the burnt offerings on the bronze altar in the courtyard (Exodus 27:1-8) and the incense on the gold altar inside the tent (Exodus 30:1-10).

decisions.choice: the holy of holies: the Most Holy Place
decisions.reason: The phrase names the inner room where the ark stood (Exodus 26:33-34). The work there was the high priest's, above all on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16). The same words can mean "the most holy things" (Numbers 4:4), but the setting beside atonement points to the place.

decisions.choice: make atonement for Israel
decisions.reason: Through the offerings the priests made, the sins of Israel were covered and the people made right with God (Leviticus 16:32-34).

decisions.choice: the slave of God: Moses' title of honor
decisions.reason: The word names a person who belongs to a master and serves him, not a hired worker. Said of Moses it is a title of honor (Numbers 12:7; Deuteronomy 34:5; Joshua 1:1). The priests' work followed what the LORD had commanded through him.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere for Moses, Literal keeps "slave" to show the word's hard edge, and Balanced and Readable say "servant", the fitting word for a trusted man in his master's service.

decisions.choice: [offerings]; made the offerings go up in smoke (Balanced); burned the offerings ... burned incense (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb has no object. Literal supplies "offerings" in brackets and Balanced keeps the picture of the smoke; Readable names what was burned on each altar.

decisions.choice: dwelling places ... encampments: the Levites' settlements

decisions.choice: for theirs was the lot: the first lot, as in Joshua 21:10
decisions.reason: From here to verse 66 the chapter follows the list of Levite towns in Joshua 21:10-39, sometimes with other names or fewer towns. decisions.choice: the priests first, then the rest of the Levites
decisions.reason: Joshua gives the totals for each Levite group before the towns (Joshua 21:4-8); Chronicles names the priests' towns first (verses 40-45) and then gives the totals and the other towns (verses 46-66).

decisions.choice: the Levites; first
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are and adds "first" from the sense of the lot (m2; Joshua 21:10). The other levels keep the shorter wording.

decisions.choice: To the descendants of Aaron ... the lot fell.
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the priests first, as the Hebrew does, and ends with the lot.

decisions.choice: Hilez (the Leningrad Codex)
decisions.reason: The Leningrad Codex, the manuscript on which the printed Hebrew text is based, spells this name Hilez; other Hebrew manuscripts and printed editions have Hilen. Joshua 21:15 has Holon, a town of Judah (Joshua 15:51), and the names probably refer to the same place. The Leningrad spelling is followed, though the other spelling may be the original.

en.L: And to the sons of Kohath who remained, from the clan of the tribe, from the half of the tribe, half Manasseh, by lot, ten cities.
en.B: The rest of the descendants of Kohath received ten towns by lot from the clan of the tribe and from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
en.R: The rest of Kohath's descendants received ten towns by lot from the tribes, including half the tribe of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: the clan of the tribe: the name of the tribe seems to be missing
alternatives: from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim and from the tribe of Dan and from the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 21:5)
decisions.reason: Joshua 21:5 reads "from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim and from the tribe of Dan and from the half of the tribe of Manasseh". Here "the tribe" has no name, and Ephraim and Dan are missing, probably lost in copying when the eye skipped from one "tribe" to the next. Verses 51-55 show that the ten towns came from Ephraim as well as Manasseh. The Hebrew text as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: the remaining: the Kohathites who were not priests
decisions.reason: As in Joshua 21:5: the descendants of Aaron have been dealt with, and "the rest" are the other Kohathite families.

decisions.choice: from the tribes, including half the tribe of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Readable does not leave "the tribe" without a name; it speaks of the tribes in general and names Manasseh, as verses 51-55 bear out (m1).

decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it is an impersonal way of saying the towns are named one by one, as in Joshua 21:9.

decisions.choice: that have been listed by name

decisions.reason: Helkath is in Asher's lot (Joshua 19:25). The Hukok of Joshua 19:34 lay on Naphtali's border; whether the same place is meant here is not clear.

records.literal_gloss: And from [the] tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee and its pasture lands, and Hammon and its pasture lands, and Kiriathaim and its pasture lands.

en.L: And from the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee and its pasturelands, and Hammon and its pasturelands, and Kiriathaim and its pasturelands.
en.B: From the tribe of Naphtali they gave Kedesh in Galilee and its pasturelands, Hammon and its pasturelands, and Kiriathaim and its pasturelands.
en.R: From the tribe of Naphtali they gave Kedesh in Galilee and its pasturelands, Hammon and its pasturelands, and Kiriathaim and its pasturelands.

decisions.choice: Kedesh, Hammon and Kiriathaim: as in Joshua 21:32, where they are Kedesh, Hammoth-dor and Kartan
decisions.reason: Kedesh in Galilee was a city of refuge (Joshua 20:7; 21:32), though Chronicles does not repeat the title. Hammon is the Hammoth-dor of Joshua, a name from a word for hot springs. Kiriathaim stands where Joshua has Kartan; both may come from a word for "town".

decisions.choice: they gave / they received
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the towns without repeating the verb, as in Joshua 21:17.

records.literal_gloss: To [the] sons of Merari the remaining, from [the] tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono and its pasture lands, Tabor and its pasture lands.

en.L: To the sons of Merari who remained, from the tribe of Zebulun: Rimmono and its pasturelands, Tabor and its pasturelands.
en.B: To the descendants of Merari, the remaining Levites, they gave from the tribe of Zebulun Rimmono and its pasturelands, and Tabor and its pasturelands.
en.R: Merari's descendants, the rest of the Levites, received Rimmono and its pasturelands, and Tabor and its pasturelands, from the tribe of Zebulun.

decisions.choice: the remaining: the last of the Levite groups
decisions.reason: As in Joshua 21:34, Merari's clans are "the rest" of the Levites, after the priests, the other Kohathites and the Gershomites.

decisions.choice: Rimmono and Tabor: Joshua 21:34-35 names four other towns
decisions.reason: Joshua lists Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah and Nahalal from Zebulun. Rimmono is probably the Rimmon of Joshua 19:13, and perhaps Joshua's Dimnah. Tabor may be the town on the border near Mount Tabor (Joshua 19:22).

decisions.choice: the remaining Levites / the rest of the Levites; they gave / received
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom "the remaining" refers to, as Joshua 21:34 does, and supply the verb.

records.literal_gloss: And from beyond [the] Jordan of Jericho, to [the] east of the Jordan, from [the] tribe of Reuben, Bezer in the wilderness and its pasture lands, and Jahaz and its pasture lands,

en.L: And from across the Jordan at Jericho, on the east of the Jordan, from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the wilderness and its pasturelands, and Jahaz and its pasturelands,
en.B: Across the Jordan from Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, they gave from the tribe of Reuben Bezer in the wilderness and its pasturelands, Jahaz and its pasturelands,
en.R: On the east side of the Jordan River, across from Jericho, they gave from the tribe of Reuben Bezer in the wilderness and its pasturelands, and Jahaz and its pasturelands.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan at Jericho: the land east of the river, opposite Jericho
decisions.reason: "The Jordan of Jericho" is the stretch of the river by Jericho (Numbers 22:1; 26:3). "Across the Jordan" speaks from the land west of it, and the writer adds "to the east of the Jordan" to make the side plain.

decisions.choice: Bezer in the wilderness and Jahaz: as in Joshua 21:36
decisions.reason: Bezer was the southern city of refuge east of the Jordan (Deuteronomy 4:43; Joshua 20:8). Jahaz is where Israel defeated Sihon (Numbers 21:23-24). The Leningrad Codex lacks Joshua 21:36-37, but these Reubenite towns stand in the Hebrew of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: they gave
decisions.reason: As in verse 57.

decisions.choice: Kedemoth and Mephaath: towns of Reuben
decisions.reason: Both are named in Reuben's land (Joshua 13:18) and in Joshua 21:37.

decisions.choice: Ramoth in Gilead and Mahanaim: as in Joshua 21:38
decisions.reason: Ramoth in Gilead was a city of refuge (Deuteronomy 4:43; Joshua 20:8; 21:38), though Chronicles does not repeat the title. Mahanaim lay on the border of Gad (Joshua 13:26).

decisions.choice: Heshbon and Jazer: as in Joshua 21:39
decisions.reason: Heshbon had been Sihon's royal city (Joshua 12:2), and Jazer is named in Gad's land (Joshua 13:25). The list ends here, without the totals and summary of Joshua 21:40-42.
